headline: Highest risk is medium: LightAgent can ingest and act on Superset outputs via shared APIs, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct evidence of shared storage or locked coordination.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use browsers, MCP, and OpenAI-compatible APIs, so it may ingest external content or tool outputs as instructions. Superset exposes an API and can produce dashboard/query content that LightAgent could consume. No shared filesystem is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF LightAgent reads Superset-rendered content or API responses as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through copy-paste, browser automation, or MCP payloads, attacker-controlled text can bridge the agents.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on any Superset-derived text.
Add provenance tags to all Superset outputs before LightAgent consumes them.
Use a read-only account for Superset API access.
Require a human review step for any browser-sourced content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the orchestration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool calls, and tool results, while Superset has only allowlisted egress and no sensitive data classes are listed. There is no documented shared workspace or common OAuth principal, so leakage is plausible but not evidenced as a default path.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same workspace or clipboard bridge, LightAgent data can be exposed to Superset workflows.
IF Superset is configured to ingest LightAgent logs or traces, sensitive conversation data may flow outward.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Do not share clipboard or filesystem mounts between them.
Restrict Superset to non-sensitive datasets.
Review outbound destinations on both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports subprocesses, browsers, MCP, and multiple instances; Superset exposes an API and is runnable false in the profile, so direct write contention is not documented. Still, overlapping API-driven workflows can conflict on shared mutable resources if orchestrated together, and uncertainty prevents a low rating.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external dataset, dashboard, or config store, race conditions can occur.
IF the orchestrator launches multiple LightAgent instances against the same Superset resource, state conflicts become likely.
mitigations: Assign separate mutable resources to each agent.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Use per-agent API tokens with least privilege.
Turn off concurrent writes during shared workflows.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can generate tool outputs and workflow state that Superset may consume through APIs or downstream analytics flows. Superset is a data-engineering/BI system, so if it treats LightAgent output as authoritative, errors can propagate into reports or actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF Superset ingests LightAgent-generated facts without validation, incorrect outputs can cascade into dashboards or decisions.
IF LightAgent is used to summarize or transform data for Superset, any hallucination can be amplified downstream.
mitigations: Require source links for any LightAgent-produced facts.
Add a validation step before Superset ingestion.
Limit LightAgent to drafting, not publishing.
Flag low-confidence outputs for review.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles API keys and long-term memory, while Superset lists no special compliance scope or residency constraints. The profiles do not show a mismatch like PHI or EU PII flow, so only a small compliance gap is visible from documentation alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through LightAgent memory or traces, retention obligations may be affected.
IF Superset is deployed under stricter residency or retention rules than LightAgent, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in LightAgent memory.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Use separate environments for regulated and unregulated data.
Review logging defaults before deployment.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
